before.definition: A named tool that does a task. You can give it values to use, and it can give a result back.

after.definition: A reusable block of code that can receive inputs, perform a task, and give back a result. Functions can have names or be unnamed.

after.label: Collection index
after.context: Position in a list, array, or similar collection. A database index is a different meaning of index.

after.label: Database index
after.context: Database lookup structure, not an item’s position in an array.

after.label: Class (object-oriented programming)
after.context: A programming type or template for objects. An HTML/CSS class is a different use of the word.

after.label: HTML/CSS class
after.context: A reusable label on HTML elements, not an object-oriented class definition.

after.label: TypeScript interface
after.context: This entry describes a TypeScript type contract. In everyday software discussion, interface can also mean a screen or a boundary between systems.

after.label: Swift protocol
after.context: This entry describes Swift type requirements. A network protocol instead specifies communication rules.

after.label: Swift optional
after.context: This entry describes Swift’s value-or-nil type, not merely an optional task.

after.label: SQL NULL
after.context: SQL uses three-valued logic for missing/unknown values. JavaScript null and Python None have different language rules.

before.label: template literal
before.definition: Text with spaces for values that code fills in.
before.example: In Python, f"Hi {name}" puts the value of name into the message.

after.label: Text interpolation
after.definition: Building text by inserting values from expressions. Each programming language has its own syntax for this.
after.example: Python: f"Hi {name}". JavaScript: `Hi ${name}`. Both insert name, but their quote marks and braces differ.
after.context: A JavaScript template literal and a Python f-string are related tools, not interchangeable syntax.

before.definition: Code that prepares a new object when it is created.
before.example: In Python, __init__ sets up an object’s starting data.

after.definition: Code used when creating an object to prepare its starting state.
after.example: In Python, __init__ initializes an instance after it has been created.
after.context: Languages separate allocation and initialization in different ways; __init__ is not Python’s object-allocation method.
The meaning depends on context: a code token, a model’s text token, and an access token are different things. An access token may be a credential; never paste one into public examples.
AI model is the broad term. A language model, including a large language model (LLM), is one kind; not every AI model generates language.
